cells: @mode NAIVE (Linear Vertex Interpolation) @concept Linearly interpolates corresponding vertex attributes (positions, normals, UVs) directly between two static target buffers using standard linear mix: P_final = (1 - t) * P_A + t * P_B @requirements Requires Mesh A and Mesh B to share the exact same vertex count and index topology (e.g., blendshapes/morph targets for facial animation). @pros Extremely fast, minimal GPU memory overhead, standard in game pipelines. @cons Strictly fails on models with differing vertex counts or different structures. [Source line 24](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/3d/MorphOptions.ts#L24).

@mode SWARM (Gaussian Splat / Particle-Based Fluidic Morph) @concept Dissolves both Mesh A and Mesh B into a dense point cloud of volumetric grains. Triangle surface sampling is used to equalize the vertex count, and Morton space-curves (Z-sorting) are used to pair adjacent vertices geographically. The transition is computed via continuous low-frequency wind turbulence (Curl Noise), and the result is rendered as billboarded Gaussian Splats. @requirements Requires pre-sampling meshes to an identical vertex count and sorting on the CPU. @pros Can morph between *any* two arbitrary 3D models seamlessly. @cons Destroys solid triangle surfaces during transition; suited for particle effects. [Source line 42](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/3d/MorphOptions.ts#L42).

@mode SDF_VOLUMETRIC (Signed Distance Field + Marching Cubes Isosurface) @concept Discretizes the 3D space into a voxel grid. We compute a Signed Distance Field for both meshes where each voxel stores the distance to the nearest triangle. These grids are interpolated on the GPU, and a Marching Cubes compute pass extracts the triangulated boundary (the zero-isosurface) dynamically. @requirements Requires 3D storage textures and a Marching Cubes edge-lookup table on the GPU. @pros The holy grail of organic morphs.
